'''Esperança Maria Eduardo Francisco da Costa''' (born 3 May 1961) is an Angolan biologist, university researcher-teacher and politician who is currently serving as the fourth [[vice president of Angola]] since 15 September 2022.<ref name="jstor">[https://plants.jstor.org/stable/10.5555/al.ap.person.bm000500269 Costa, Esperança Maria Eduardo Francisco da (1961-)]. JSTOR Global Plants. 2000.</ref>

She was the deputy head of the [[Popular Movement for the Liberation of Angola]] (MPLA) party for the [[2022 Angolan general election]]s.<ref>[https://luandapost.com/quem-e-esperanca-eduardo-francisco-da-costa-a-futura-vice-presidente-de-angola/ Quem é Esperança Eduardo Francisco da Costa, a futura Vice-Presidente de Angola] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221230230244/https://luandapost.com/quem-e-esperanca-eduardo-francisco-da-costa-a-futura-vice-presidente-de-angola/ |date=30 December 2022 }}. Luanda Post. 23 de maio de 2022.</ref> With the party's victory, she became Vice President of Angola on 15 September 2022.<ref name="RNA 15-9-22">[https://rna.ao/rna.ao/2022/09/15/investidura-do-presidente-da-republica/ Investidura do Presidente da República]. Rádio Nacional de Angola. 15 de setembro de 2022.</ref><ref name="observador 29-8-22">[https://observador.pt/2022/08/29/cne-angolana-divulga-resultados-definitivos-e-proclama-joao-lourenco-como-presidente-de-angola/ CNE angolana divulga resultados definitivos e proclama João Lourenço como Presidente de Angola]. Observador. 29 de agosto de 2022.</ref>

== Biography ==

Esperança da Costa was born in [[Luanda]], Angola, on 3 May 1961.<ref name="SABONET">{{cite web|url=https://www.sanbi.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/04/sabonetnewsvol53.pdf |title=Profile: Esperança da Costa |website=SABONET News / Southern African Botanical Diversity Network Project |volume=5 |number=3 |date=December 2000}}</ref><ref name="jstor"/> In her youth, during the country's decolonization process, she was part of the [[Youth of MPLA|Youth Movement of the Popular Movement for the Liberation of Angola]] (JMPLA) and the [[Organization of Angolan Women]] (OMA).<ref name="JA 4-6-22">[https://www.jornaldeangola.ao/ao/noticias/esperanca-da-costa-as-mulheres-estao-prontas-para-os-desafios/ Esperança da Costa: "As mulheres estão prontas para os desafios"]. Jornal de Angola. 4 de junho de 2022.</ref>

=== Scientific career ===
She studied biology at [[Agostinho Neto University]] (UAN), graduating in 1985. Between 1983 and 1984, she specialized at the Botany Center of the Tropical Scientific Research Institute in [[Lisbon, Portugal]].<ref name="jstor"/>

When she returned to Luanda, she was appointed assistant in plant biology at [[Agostinho Neto University]] (UAN), becoming head of the biology department in 1986. Between 1986 and 1990, she was responsible for the development of the Luanda Herbarium.<ref name="jstor"/>

In 1990, she began her master's degree in plant productivity at the [[Technical University of Lisbon]], followed, in 1992, to a doctorate in [[phytoecology]]<ref name="JA 4-6-22" /> at the same university, completed in 1997.<ref name="jstor"/>

Upon returning to Angola, she was readmitted as a professor at Agostinho Neto University, becoming director of the Luanda Herbarium and assistant professor of plant biology.<ref>[https://www.dw.com/pt-002/ilustre-desconhecida-%C3%A9-candidata-do-mpla-a-vice-presidente/a-61920072 "Ilustre desconhecida" é candidata do MPLA a vice-Presidente]. DW. 24 de maio de 2022.</ref>

She then served as vice-director of Scientific Affairs and, from 2002, vice-rector for University Expansion at UAN until 2007. Between 2007 and 2010, she was the National Director of the Expansion of Higher Education at the Ministry of Higher Education, supervising the national construction of campuses and new higher education institutions. She acted as director of the UAN Botany Center between 2010 and 2020.<ref name="JA 4-6-22" />

=== Political career  ===
She was elected to the Central Committee of the Popular Movement for the Liberation of Angola (MPLA) in 2019, being appointed by President [[João Lourenço]] as Secretary of State of Fishing in 2020.<ref name="JA 4-6-22" />

==Vice President of Angola (2022-present)==
She contested and won the [[2022 Angolan general election]]s as the [[running mate]] of [[João Lourenço]].<ref name="observador 29-8-22"/> She assumed office as Vice President of Angola on 15 September 2022.<ref name="RNA 15-9-22"/>
